insights.claim: The training server uses emptyDir volumes for model storage, making trained models ephemeral and introducing a cold-start period after pod restarts where latency predictions are unavailable until sufficient data is re-accumulated and models are retrained.
insights.reasoning: The training server stores models in an emptyDir volume (deploy/base/training/deployment.yaml:58-62) and requires MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_RETRAIN (default 1000) samples before retraining. A restart loses all accumulated data and models, leaving prediction servers without valid models until the training server re-accumulates enough data from the llm-d gateway.

insights.claim: Neither server implements application-level authentication, relying entirely on network-level isolation for access control across all 24 HTTP endpoints including model management and training data ingestion APIs.
insights.reasoning: The analyzer detected no auth middleware in the FastAPI applications, confirmed by source inspection of both server imports. The /add_training_data_bulk endpoint accepts arbitrary latency data without authentication, meaning any pod with network access to the training service could inject poisoned training data and degrade prediction quality.

insights.claim: The prediction server uses polling-based model synchronization (default 10s interval) rather than push-based notification, introducing bounded staleness in latency predictions after model retraining.
insights.reasoning: The prediction server periodically downloads models via HTTP from the training server at a configurable interval (MODEL_SYNC_INTERVAL_SEC=10). This avoids the complexity of shared volumes or event-driven model distribution but means predictions can be up to 10 seconds stale after a model retrain. The 10-replica prediction deployment multiplied by 10s polling creates steady background traffic to the single-replica training server.
